$comment: THE ONE SOURCE. Product brief section 2.6: the palette, type scale,
spacing scale and radii live in one file and are exported to CSS custom
properties and to Dart constants by a build step. Neither client
hardcodes a colour.
That is not tidiness. Two clients shipping in parallel drift the moment a
hex value exists in two places, and section 0 makes it explicit: a
colour, spacing value or label that differs between web and native is a
bug. Acceptance criterion 10 is that a change here updates both.
Regenerate with:  python tools/tokens.py
Checked by:       tests/test_tokens.py, which fails if either export is
stale - so a token changed here and not exported is a
test failure rather than a visual surprise later.

core.$comment: Product brief 6.1. Six values, and no seventh without a reason written here.

etch.use: rules, borders, grid lines, inactive strokes

phosphor.use: primary accent, active state, primary actions, focused input
phosphor.why: The amber phosphor value, chosen over the obvious terminal green so the product does not read as a generic hacker skin. Green appears only as a state colour.

$comment: Product brief 6.1. USED ONLY INSIDE THE 3D CANVAS AND FOR ANNOTATION.
A plotter pen set, where different line types mean different things -
which is why these are separate from the core palette and must not be
borrowed for chrome.
Every pen is paired with an icon or a label in the UI: brief 6.7
forbids colour-only status signalling.

ref.meaning: reference body from a photo, never printed

pass.meaning: passed check, confirmed dimension, joint clearance OK

warn.meaning: tolerance risk, uncalibrated default, thin wall

fail.meaning: failed check, interpenetration, out of bed bounds
fail.why: Magenta rather than red, because it comes from the plotter pen set and because red is reserved for destructive confirmation only.

$comment: Product brief 6.2. Two families, clearly distinct, and monospace is
functional rather than decorative: parameter digits must not shift
width while a slider moves. Every numeric field sets tabular-nums.
Prose is a neutral grotesque because monospace paragraphs are hostile
to read - onboarding, errors and help are prose, not data.

mono.stack: 'IBM Plex Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
mono.use: labels, parameters, numbers, dimensions, the command line, the coordinate readout, buttons

scale.$comment: px. Sentence case throughout; no tracked-out all-caps labels.

space.$comment: px. A 4-based scale; every gap in either client is one of these.

radius.$comment: px. Squared-off rather than pill-shaped: this is a machine, not a toy.

$comment: Non-visual constants the brief pins, kept here so neither client
invents one. `tap` is brief 6.3's one-handed requirement; `min_width`
is brief 6.7's quality floor.
